sample.name: Cloud Service Provider
sample.description:
The Cloud Service Provider hosts the core operational systems on which day-to-day delivery depends — registration, records and analytics workloads run on their managed infrastructure under a shared-responsibility model.

As an interested party they materially shape our information-security, availability and privacy posture, so the relationship is governed through a signed master agreement, a data-processing addendum and an agreed service-level commitment:

• Availability & resilience — the provider must sustain the contracted uptime, maintain multi-zone redundancy, and give advance notice of maintenance windows that could affect service.
• Security controls — platform hardening, encryption in transit and at rest, key management and access logging are the provider’s responsibility; tenant configuration remains ours.
• Privacy & data residency — customer personal data must be processed only within approved jurisdictions, with sub-processors disclosed and subject to review.
• Incident handling — security incidents and outages must be communicated promptly, with root-cause analysis and remediation timelines.

The relationship is reviewed at each management review and whenever the provider changes sub-processors, regions or certification status.

comments.author: Jennifer Susan Walters
comments.text: Adding the Cloud Service Provider as a formal interested party — they now host our core workloads, so their requirements need to be tracked and reviewed.

comments.author: Peter Parker
comments.text: Agreed. Their availability commitment and incident-notification terms are the ones I care about most from a security angle.

comments.author: Monica Rambeau
comments.text: Do we have the current data-processing addendum on file? We can’t assert privacy compliance without the sub-processor list.

comments.author: Jennifer Susan Walters
comments.text: DPA is signed; I’ll attach the latest sub-processor disclosure to the Data processing requirement.

comments.author: Matthew Michael Murdock
comments.text: Legal view: confirm the contracted processing regions match our approved-jurisdictions list before we mark that requirement addressed.

comments.author: Wanda Maximoff
comments.text: Operations note — last quarter they had two short outages. Incident-notification timeliness should be part of our evaluation.

comments.author: Peter Parker
comments.text: The incident-notification requirement is now Addressed — contract terms updated to a 24-hour breach-reporting window.

comments.author: Monica Rambeau
comments.text: Good. Exit and portability still worries me — we need a documented data-return format before we deepen reliance.

comments.author: Jennifer Susan Walters
comments.text: Raised the Exit / portability requirement as Open; owner assigned to draft the transition plan.

comments.author: Matthew Michael Murdock
comments.text: Certification requirement on hold until their next audit report is published — expected next month.

comments.author: Wanda Maximoff
comments.text: They confirmed the new region is within our approved list. Updating the privacy requirement accordingly.

comments.author: Peter Parker
comments.text: Once the audit report lands we can move the certification requirement forward and close this review cycle.

comments.author: Jennifer Susan Walters
comments.text: Keeping this party under active review until the exit plan and certification evidence are both in place.
